Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Afghanistan's reply! The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Noor Ali Zadran and Ibrahim Zadran are the two openers for Afghanistan. Vishwa Fernando to start with the ball. Lets go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

With Chamika Gunasekara retired and not opting for a Concussion sub as of now, the Sri Lankan inning comes to a close on 439 for 9. The hosts now lead by 241 runs and the visitors will need to put up a performance with a bit of gritty nature to turn this around in their favor. A couple of big knocks from Angelo Mathews and Dhananjaya de Silva has helped the hosts achieve this lead as they now hold a firm grip on this game and would be dictating terms.

Naveed Zadran was brilliant and aggressive to start the day with the ball as he removed a couple and it was his delivery that hit Chamika Gunasekara on the helmet forcing him to retire. Nijat Masood took a wicket as well this morning. The bowlers managed to wrap up things with Naveed Zadran picking up 4 in total while Qais Ahmad and Nijat Masood picked up a couple each.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all in readiness to begin proceedings on Day 3. Sadeera Samarawickrama will be accompanied by Chamika Gunasekara as the Lankan batters march out to bat. Qais Ahmad will begin to complete the remaining 4 deliveries.

Angelo Mathews is up for a quick chat and he says he is happy with his batting but gutted with how he got out. Adds that he and Dinesh Chandimal took their time and played every ball to its merit as they planned to put away bad deliveries but they were presented very less in number by the Afghanistan bowlers.

The visitors though would look to bundle the Lankans as early as they can so they do not fall further behind in the game. The onus would be on Qais Ahmad, Naveed Zadran and Zia ur Rehman to give the sides crucial breakthroughs and wrap the Lankan innings up quickly. With the wicket starting to assist the spinner, bowlers like Qais Ahmad and Zia ur Rehman become all that important now. Let's see what unfolds in the first session as these two Asian sides put up a show for all.

After a brilliant day of cricket with the bat for Lanka on day 2, Sri Lanka are now in a dominating situation up against the Afghans. The Lankans scored 330 on day 2 and now lead Afghanistan by 212 runs. After a marathon partnership of 232 runs between Dinesh Chandimal and Angelo Mathews for the fourth wicket the side now stands a chance to extend their lead today. The Lankans are now in a commanding position and will look to stretch the lead to around 300 and then try and inflict a defeat with an innings on Afghanistan.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The key is to be positive, they should not be losing hopes as they are well behind in the game. They need quick wickets first up to get back into this one and we expect the conditions to be fine for batting on Day 3 as well and they will need to cash in. Sri Lanka on the other hand, would hope to bat as long as possible as they would be aiming to bat only once. Important day awaits. Join us for the action which will begin at 1000 IST (0430 GMT). Till then, take care and goodbye!

A day which has belonged to the hosts and they are well and truly ahead in this game! They have stretched their lead to over 200 and are still not done. That is mainly down to two men, Angelo Mathews and Dinesh Chandimal. Both added a massive partnership and both scored tons. They batted for most of the day and have taken their side well into the ascendancy. For Afghanistan it has been a real struggle, the pitch was not offering a lot and their bowlers have not bowled that well too. They were quite wayward and offered far too many boundary balls. They would be pleased that the day has come to an end but they need a really good Day 3 to get back into the game.

He pulls it hard through square leg but could not stop his bat swing and it hits the stumps. Unfortunate but end of a brilliant knock. THAT WILL ALSO BE STUMPS!

It is hard work for them out there and all they can do for now is be patient. Can someone from their side put in a whole-hearted performance and get their side back in the game? A solid session for the hosts as they have scored 97 runs. Despite losing three wickets they have batted well and are just trailing by 21 runs. Dimuth Karunaratne continued from where he left off as he scored few boundaries and reached to his fifty. Nishan Madushka and Kusal Mendis fell in quick succession but Angelo Mathews and Dinesh Chandimal have built yet another session. A partnership of 29 runs and Sri Lanka will hope it grows more. Afghanistan, on the flip side were decent with the ball. They lacked discipline but somehow got three wickets. They will hope to get better and make sure they don't give any easy runs in the next session. Join us back in a while.

Rahmat was doing all the work but once he fell, Afghanistan fumbled and got all out under 200. In reply, Sri Lanka scalped half the deficit in the last session. Right then, Sri Lanka trail by 118 runs. The surface is about to play better on the second day, and with Sri Lanka's experienced batters like Dinesh Chandimal and Angelo Mathews still to come to bat, Afghanistan would surely be raring to have early breakthroughs on Day 2 and restrict the hosts from taking a broad lead. Day 2 will commence at 10 am IST (4.30 am GMT) on Saturday, but you can join us earlier for the build-up. Take care, cheers!

Sri Lanka, in response, got off to a promising start with Asitha Fernando dismissing Ibrahim Zadran early on. Despite the spin and the swing vanishing away after the first half hour or so, Vishwa Fernando's return to the attack proved decisive as he removed Noor Ali, disrupting a growing partnership. Prabath Jayasuriya also made significant contributions, clinching a three-wicket haul. Sri Lanka's bowlers tightened their grip, preventing partnerships from flourishing during the second session. Both Vishwa and Asitha made crucial breakthroughs in the Afghan middle order, restricting them below the 200-run mark. Sri Lanka began their innings aggressively with Karunaratne and Madushka, and they ended the day with a promising total on the board. With experienced players yet to bat, Sri Lanka aims to extend their lead as much as possible on Day 2.

Earlier in the day, Sri Lanka opted to bowl first and invited Afghanistan to bat, who had a rocky start with Ibrahim Zadran departing in the second delivery of the match. Rahmat Shah and debutant Noor Ali Zadran then built a brisk partnership of 57 runs before Noor's dismissal. Despite Rahmat's resilience, Afghanistan suffered a dramatic collapse in the second session, losing wickets in quick succession.
